metadata.description: Plugins for people building with AI who aren't systems engineers.

plugins.name: guardrails
plugins.description: Blocks commits to protected branches and irreversible deletes, and flags prompt injection in content the model reads or writes.

plugins.name: git-hygiene
plugins.description: Tells you which old branches are safe to delete and which still hold work that exists nowhere else, then cleans up the safe ones once you approve them. Never deletes unmerged commits.

plugins.name: build-loop
plugins.description: Keep everything you build honest. Log what a skill, hook, command, plugin or script got wrong the moment it happens, fix it from the queue with an approval gate, know what else the fix puts at risk, and keep a to-build list that closes itself when the work actually ships.

plugins.name: slop-check
plugins.description: Catch the habits that mean nobody edited it. Blocks em dashes and choppy sentence runs in the assistant's own writing, and checks any draft, document, pull request, chart or spec for the signs it shipped unreviewed.

plugins.name: session
plugins.description: Make sessions continuous. Wrap one up into a handoff the next one loads, start with today's date and a compact build-loop brief, warn when another session is already working here, and put cost, context and connected tool health in the status line.

plugins.name: ip-inventory
plugins.description: Checks a record of what you have built against GitHub and your disk, reports what has drifted, and turns the result into the schedule of prior IP you attach to an employment agreement.

plugins.name: spend-guardrails
plugins.description: Choose the lowest-cost current Claude or OpenAI model that can reliably do the work, without recommending retired models.
